The '''1902 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 16th staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament.

[[London GAA|London]] were the [[1901 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.londongaa.org/news-details/10070028/|title=London 125: All-Ireland win of 1901|publisher=London GAA website|date=18 March 2021|accessdate=31 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theirishworld.com/the-game-of-their-lives/|title=The game of their lives|publisher=The Irish World|date=15 October 2024|accessdate=31 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://hoganstand.com/article/index/316325|title=London unveil commemorative 125th anniversary jerseys inspired by All-Ireland win|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=3 April 2021|accessdate=31 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref>

The [[#All-Ireland final|All-Ireland final]] was played on 11 September 1904 at the [[Cork Athletic Grounds|Athletic Grounds]] in [[Cork (city)|Cork]], between [[Cork GAA|Cork]] and London, in what was their second consecutive meeting in the All-Ireland final. Cork won the match by 3–13 to 0–00 to claim their fifth All-Ireland title overall and a first title in [[1894 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|eight years]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20369932.html|title=Driven Dungourney’s hi-tech edge to help against Fenor|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=5 December 2015|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://dungourneygaa.com/about-us/|title=About us|publisher=Dungourney GAA website|date=|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corknews/arid-41668541.html|title=Nostalgia: Cork hurling remains a constant in a changing world|publisher=Echo Live|date=13 July 2025|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref>

==Championship statistics==
===Miscellaneous===

* [[Derry GAA|Derry]] win the [[Ulster Senior Hurling Championship|Ulster championship]] for the first time.
* The newly opened [[Cork Athletic Grounds]] hosted the All-Ireland final for the first time.
